data.title: Mach Travel Solutions Surpasses 200 Active Corporate Clients; Plans Expansion into Pune, Chennai and Hyderabad
data.description:
Corporate client base surpasses 200; planned FY27 expansion would extend operational presence to 10 cities

NEW DELHI, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Mach Travel Solutions Limited (), a publicly listed technology-enabled travel solutions company, announced that it has crossed 200 active transacting corporate clients for its Corporate Ticketing and Self-Booking Tool (SBT) services. It also plans to establish operations in Pune, Chennai and Hyderabad during FY27, extending its operational presence to ten cities upon completion.

Since launching its dedicated Corporate Travel vertical in April 2026, Mach has reached this milestone in approximately eight months, up from 140+ corporate clients reported as of September 30, 2026. This progression demonstrates continued enterprise client acquisition and transaction activity.

Strengthening the Corporate Travel Business

Mach's Corporate Travel offering combines its Self-Booking Tool with dedicated account management, structured booking workflows, approval mechanisms and centralised travel processes, helping businesses manage travel requirements efficiently.

Its active corporate clients span Automotive & Engineering, Cement & Building Materials, Chemicals, Pharmaceuticals, Financial Services, Technology & IT, Electronics, Aviation, Media & Entertainment, Education, Healthcare, FMCG, Infrastructure, Consumer Products, Textiles and Industrials.

Corporate Travel provides opportunities for year-round transactions and long-term enterprise relationships, complementing Mach's established MICE business. The client base also creates potential for cross-selling MICE, hotel, incentive and leisure travel services, subject to individual client needs.

Planned Expansion into Three New Cities

The proposed offices in Pune, Chennai and Hyderabad would strengthen Mach's access to major corporate and industrial markets and help serve existing and prospective enterprise customers.

These locations would complement its seven existing offices in Noida, New Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Bhubaneswar and Ahmedabad, bringing the total to ten cities if the expansion is completed.

Management Commentary

Commenting on the developments, Mr. Kaushik Ghosh, Joint Managing Director, Mach Travel Solutions Limited, said:

"Crossing 200 active transacting corporate clients within eight months of launching our dedicated Corporate Travel vertical is an important milestone and reflects the growing acceptance of our technology-enabled travel management solutions.

Our planned expansion into Pune, Chennai and Hyderabad will further strengthen our presence in key corporate markets and bring us closer to our customers.

We remain focused on scaling our Corporate Travel business, strengthening client relationships and delivering sustainable long-term growth through technology and service excellence."

About Mach Travel Solutions Limited

Mach Travel Solutions Limited (formerly Mach Conferences & Events Ltd.) is a publicly listed technology-enabled travel solutions company listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange (). Incorporated in 2004, the Company provides technology-enabled end-to-end travel solutions across Corporate Travel, MICE, B2B, Leisure, Inbound Travel and Government & Institutional Projects.

The Company has a strong pan-India presence with offices in Noida, New Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Bhubaneswar and Ahmedabad, and is accredited by and associated with leading national and international travel associations, including IATA, GBTA, PATA, IATO, ADTOI, OTOAI, SKÅL International, JATA, ICPB, EGAC and NIMA.

For more information, please visit https://www.machtravelsolutions.com

The Company's B2C Online Travel Agency platform, Machtravel.com, is currently in public beta and brings together Flights, Hotels, Holidays, MICE, Cruises and Visa services.

Email: compliance@machtravel.com

Website: https://www.machtravelsolutions.com

While these forward-looking statements indicate our assessment and future expectations concerning the development of our business, several risks, uncertainties and other unknown factors could cause actual developments and results to differ materially from our expectations. These factors include, but are not limited to, general market, macro-economic, governmental and regulatory trends, movements in currency exchange and interest rates, competitive pressures, technological developments, changes in the financial conditions of third parties dealing with us, legislative developments, and other key factors that could affect our business and financial performance.

data.title: Harel Insurance Investments and Financial Services Reports Third Quarter and Nine- Month 2026 Financial Results; Achieves Record Quarterly Core Profit
data.description:
TEL AVIV, Israel, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Harel Insurance Investments and Financial Services, a leading Israeli insurance and financial group (), ("Harel Insurance Investments", "the Group" or "the Company") today reported its third quarter and first nine months 2026 results.

Highlights:

  • Core profit in Q3 2026 surpassed NIS 1 billion for the first time, setting a new quarterly record and representing a 50% increase over the past two years. Growth was driven by continued increase in insurance underwriting profit, as well as higher profits from asset management and credit activities. Core profit in the first nine months peaked at NIS 2.8 billion (First nine months of 2025: NIS 2.7 billion).
  • Comprehensive income after tax in the first nine months was NIS 2.06 billion, (First nine months of 2025: NIS 2.17 billion); ROE was 23%.
  • Comprehensive income after tax in Q3 2026 was NIS 477 million (Q3 2025: NIS 840 million), the decline in comprehensive income was due to negative nostro return; ROE was 16%.
  • Contractual Service Margin (CSM) from new sales in the first nine months of 2026 increased by 15% to NIS 1.45 billion, reflecting continuous growth in value creation in life and health insurance, which enhances future profitability. The CSM as of September 30, 2026, was NIS 17.9 billion, industry highest.
  • Total premiums, contributions and amounts received for investment contracts grew 16% to NIS 38.3 billion in the first nine months of 2026, AUM increased to NIS 654 billion as of September 30, 2026, up 15% in the past twelve months.
  • The Company's Board of Directors declared a dividend of NIS 300 million. Year-to-date, total capital returned to shareholders through dividends and share buybacks amounted to approximately NIS 1.9 billion.
  • Harel Insurance's Solvency Capital Ratio increased to 176% as of June 30, 2026, from 165% as of December 31, 2025 (including transitional measures and the Tier 2 issuance).
  • Harel Insurance's outlook revised to Positive from Stable by S&P Global Ratings, which affirmed its 'A-' long-term issuer credit and financial strength ratings.

Business performance overview:

  • Core profit after tax in Q3 2026 increased by 8% to NIS 696 million (Q3 2025: NIS 647 million).
  • Core profit after tax in the first nine months of 2026 increased by 7% to NIS 1.9 billion (First nine months of 2025: NIS 1.8 billion).

Insurance:

  • Core profit before tax from insurance activity in Q3 2026 was NIS 792 million (Q3 2025: NIS 735 million). Core profit is calculated based on an assumed annual margin of 2% and excluding special effects.
  • Core profit before tax from insurance activity in the first nine months of 2026 was NIS 2.12 billion (First nine months of 2025: NIS 2.09 billion). The increase was driven by higher core profits in life and health insurance, supported by increase in sales of growth products (life risks, medical expenses and critical illness), and was partially offset by lower core profit in non-life insurance.
  • The future value of new business (CSM new business) in the first nine months of 2026 amounted to NIS 1.45 billion, up 15% compared to the same period last year, reflecting significant value creation from the focus on growth products, which supports future profitability. Total CSM as of September 30, 2026, amounted to NIS 17.9 billion.

Asset management and credit:

  • Core profit from asset management in Q3 2026 increased 13% to NIS 120 million (Q3 2025: NIS 106 million), driven by continued growth in assets under management and management fees. The asset management segment, which includes pension and provident funds, mutual funds, ETFs and investment contracts, had assets under management of NIS 514 billion, as of September 30, 2026, an increase of NIS 79 billion in the past twelve months.
  • Core profit from the credit segment in Q3 2026 increased 11% to NIS 69 million (Q3 2025: NIS 62 million), reflecting ongoing growth in credit activity. The credit portfolio reached NIS 9.1 billion, as of September 30, 2026, an increase of NIS 2.3 billion in the past twelve months.

Overview of business segments performance

Health Insurance:

  • In Q3 2026, comprehensive income before tax was NIS 550 million (Q3 2025: NIS 605 million). In the first nine months of 2026, comprehensive income before tax was NIS 1.27 billion compared to NIS 1.16 billion in the same period last year.
  • Underwriting profit in Q3 2026 increased by 15% to NIS 373 million (Q3 2025: NIS 324 million). Underwriting profit in the first nine months of 2026 was NIS 793 compared to NIS 807 million in the same period last year.

Life Insurance:

  • In Q3 2026, comprehensive income before tax was NIS 2 million (Q3 2025: NIS 244 million). In the first nine months of 2026, comprehensive income before tax was NIS 529 million compared to NIS 792 million in the same period last year. The decline in comprehensive income was driven by lower finance and investment income.
  • Underwriting profit in Q3 2026 increased 28% to NIS 226 million (Q3 2025: NIS 177 million). Underwriting profit in the first nine months of 2026 was NIS 611 million compared to NIS 605 million in the same period last year.

Non-life Insurance:

  • In Q3 2026, comprehensive income before tax was NIS 46 million (Q3 2025: NIS 278 million). In the first nine months of 2026, comprehensive income before tax was NIS 645 million compared to NIS 858 million in the same period last year. The decline in comprehensive income reflects lower finance and investment income.
  • Underwriting profit in Q3 2026 was NIS 93 million (Q3 2025: NIS 113 million). Underwriting profit in the first nine months of 2026 was NIS 344 million, an increase of NIS 18 million from NIS 326 million in the same period last year.

Asset management (Pension, Provident, Financial Services and Investment Contracts):

  • In Q3 2026, comprehensive income before tax from pension and provident funds was NIS 59 million (Q3 2025: NIS 51 million). In the first nine months of the year, comprehensive income before tax was NIS 171 million compared to NIS 121 million in the same period last year. Results were affected by an increase in management fees driven by growth in AUM.
  • In Q3 2026 comprehensive income before tax from financial services (mutual funds, ETFs) and investment contracts was NIS 57 million (Q3 2025: NIS 51 million). In the first nine months of 2026, comprehensive income before tax from financial services (mutual funds, ETFs) and investment contracts was NIS 165 million, compared to NIS 119 million in the same period last year.
  • As of September 30, 2026, total assets under management in the asset management segment amounted to NIS 514 billion.

Credit:

  • In Q3 2026, core profit of the credit segment was NIS 69 million (Q3 2025: NIS 62 million). In the first nine months of 2026, core profit of the credit segment was NIS 209 million compared to NIS 169 million in the corresponding period last year. Profitability was supported by continued growth of the credit portfolio in development property financing, mortgages and credit to mid-sized businesses.
  • The credit portfolio amounted to NIS 9.1 billion as of September 30, 2026, compared to NIS 6.8 billion as of September 30, 2025, an increase of NIS 2.3 billion.

Conference Call information

Harel Insurance Investments will hold a conference call for analysts and investors in Hebrew on November 23, 2026, at 1 pm (Israel); 11 am (UK); dial in details: https://www.veidan-conferencing.com/harel. On the same date, prior to the conference call, an investor presentation (including an English version) will be available on the Israel Securities Authority's reporting website (MAGNA), and on the Company's Investor Relations website: https://pr.harel-group.co.il/

This press release, the Investor presentation and the conference call for analysts and investors are not exhaustive and do not replace the Company's latest financial reports, which contain all relevant information including forward-looking statements, as defined in the Israeli securities Law, and set out in the aforementioned reports, and the need to review those financial reports in full.

For more information, please visit Harel's Investor Relations website or contact us at investor.relations@harel-ins.co.il

About Harel Insurance Investments

Harel Insurance Investments and Financial Services Ltd. is a leading Israel-based insurance, financial services and asset management group, traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (). The company is Israeli largest insurer, engaged in health, life and non-life insurance, as well as in asset management – pension funds, provident funds and financial services such as mutual funds, ETFs and portfolio management, and credit activities. With assets under management of about NIS 654 billion, annual premiums and deposits inflows of NIS 45.7 billion and leading market shares across its business segments, Harel is well positioned to benefit the growing Israeli economy by leveraging its diversified business model, strong capital position, and long-standing expertise to deliver sustainable growth and resilient profitability. With a broad customer base, advanced digital capabilities, and a disciplined investment approach, Harel continues to strengthen its leadership position while creating long-term value for its stakeholders.

data.title: Citi Trims Ether Forecast by 6% — Market Talk
data.description:
0540 GMT - Citi cut its price target for ether to $2,838 from $3,028 as outflows from exchange-traded funds persist. Citi's Alex Saunders says ether ETFs have seen net outflows of roughly $4.5 billion since the beginning of October, while posting negative flows in each of the past seven weeks. "Total crypto market capitalization has fallen to the low end of its one-year range, and the sell-off hit ether hardest," Saunders says. Ether is 0.7% higher at $1,731.97. (joseph.wilkins@wsj.com)

0529 GMT - Citi lowered its 12-month bitcoin forecast to $99,532 from $113,000 on lower exchange-traded fund demand and a tighter macroeconomic backdrop. Citi's Alex Saunders says ETF demand has deteriorated, as bitcoin slips back into year-to-date outflows. A stronger dollar, higher real yields and a spike in equity volatility were another reason why the bank cut its flows forecast from upside to neutral. "Capital appears to be leaving the ecosystem, leaving near-term direction tied to macro rather than crypto-specific catalysts," he writes. Bitcoin is 0.8% higher at $61,367. (joseph.wilkins@wsj.com)

0421 GMT - Bitcoin edges higher in Asia after another punishing selloff over the weekend brought it to its lowest in over two years. The cryptocurrency's rebound shows that buyers were willing to return when the price fell to near $55,000, says Linh Tran at XS.com. But expectations of interest-rate hikes, a still-strong dollar and continued ETF outflows keep the outlook cautious. Over the next few sessions, Tran leans toward Bitcoin trading around $60,000. It will likely struggle to return to the $65,000 area anytime soon. If Bitcoin can hold above $60,000 through the U.S. sessions early this week--especially if ETFs are still seeing outflows--that would show that buying is strong enough to absorb the selling, Tran says. Bitcoin is up 0.6% at $61,236. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)

0412 GMT - The dollar is likely to trade around 160.00 yen throughout 2027, Morgan Stanley says in a note. Elevated Fed terminal-rate pricing and improving risk sentiment should support the dollar against the yen, while repeated verbal intervention by Japanese financial authorities should limit the yen's depreciation, the U.S. bank says. Japan's terms of trade are also expected to improve gradually next year, supporting the yen, Morgan Stanley says. A sustained downtrend in the dollar would require markets to price U.S. disinflation and a subsequent Fed easing cycle with greater conviction, the bank says. The dollar is at Y159.01. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com; @kosakunarioka)

0408 GMT - The Bank of Korea is expected to hike rates on Thursday in a likely unanimous decision, says BofA Global Research in a report. With headline inflation running above 2.5%, the case for the BOK to consider further tightening to contain inflationary pressures remains strong. Korea's widening current account surplus continues to support the won, but persistent selling by foreign equity investors has weighed on the domestic market with the benchmark Kospi struggling to hold above 5000. The BOK's 2027 GDP growth forecast will be a key figure to watch. "An upgrade to above 3.5% would signal a more bullish assessment of the ongoing semiconductor upcycle and potentially point to greater risk of further rate hikes, implying a more hawkish policy stance than we currently expect," it adds. (monica.gupta@wsj.com)

0323 GMT - Singapore's industrial production growth likely moderated in October, reflecting high base effects, DBS economists say in a note. The city-state's output surged by 15% on year during the same period last year, marking its strongest monthly gain in 2025, they note.Robust artificial intelligence-related demand likely supported precision engineering and electronics production, although electronics growth may have moderated, the economists say. DBS expects Singapore's industrial production growth to slow to 1.0% in October from 3.4% in September. The data is due later this week.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)

0240 GMT - The Singapore dollar consolidates against its U.S. counterpart in the Asian session but may be weighed by risk-off sentiment spurred by regional equity-market weakness. There are "concerns over elevated interest rates, persistent inflation pressures and the unwinding of crowded AI-related positions," UOB Global Economics & Markets Research says in a report. Based on technical analysis, however, the U.S. dollar-Singapore dollar pair's upward momentum has faded following its recent pullback, two members of the research team note. The U.S. dollar has probably entered a range-trading phase between S$1.2885 and S$1.2915, they add. The U.S. dollar is little changed at 1.2898 Singapore dollars, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

0229 GMT - Malaysia's exports could continue to remain resilient in 1Q 2027, supported by sustained AI-driven demand for electrical and electronic products and stronger energy shipments, says CGS International economist Mas Aida Che Mansor in a note. Global semiconductor sales are forecast to grow 29% in 2027. Domestic electrical and electronics capacity utilization of 87.7% also points to continued shipment growth despite rising base effects, she reckons. Petroleum and liquefied natural gas exports should provide additional support, driven by regional demand and resilient manufacturing activity in China and the Asean region. However, a sharper slowdown in the U.S. or China, weaker crude oil prices and rising trade protectionism could weigh on shipments, she adds. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)

0206 GMT - There are good reasons to believe that Australia's current housing market downturn is different to the garden variety cyclical downswings of recent decades, says Paul Bloxham, chief economist for Australia at HSBC. The decline so far is already bigger and sharper than the previous ones, while core inflation remains elevated, despite aggressive interest rate increases this year, he adds. Near-term interest rate cuts are not on the agenda while tax changes and the likelihood that global rates will stay high for longer are adding to the grim picture. Bloxham expects a 13% peak-to-trough house price fall. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)

0145 GMT - There could come a moment of acute discomfort for Australia money markets on Wednesday if inflation data for October delivers a higher-than-expected shock. Headline inflation is expected to rise to an uncomfortable 4.7%, but the more important trimmed mean measure is forecast to be little changed, landing at around 3.6% year over year. With recent economic data coming in weak, markets are already starting to price in interest-rate cuts next year, so an upward inflation shock would trigger volatility. Reserve Bank of Australia Gov. Michele Bullock said last week inflation risks remain skewed toward a rise. Central bank rhetoric remains hawkish generally. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)

0125 GMT - The rates shock has likely evolved into a growth shock, two strategists at OCBC Group Research say in a note. The "AI de-risking hits equities, EM carry and metals," the strategists say. Worries over the artificial-intelligence investment cycle have driven equities and U.S. yields lower, shifting the brunt of U.S. dollar strength toward emerging-market currencies, the strategists say. "In the near term, the USD should continue to benefit from hawkish Fed risks and the pressure that tighter global financial conditions place on the rest of the world," the strategists add. The U.S. Dollar Index is little changed at 103.763, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)

0108 GMT - Voters in Australia's southern state of Victoria are expected to hand the current Labor government a huge defeat at elections on Saturday. The mood is grim for the party, and if the drubbing is delivered, questions will be asked about what it means for the federal Labor government. It is likely to officially establish the right-wing populist One Nation party as a force that could impact the status quo in the federal arena. History has shown that voters can vote one way at state level and then another at federal elections. But Saturday's poll feels like it will be a watershed in Australian politics and the fallout could have big ramifications.(james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)

data.title: Indonesia president to nominate VP candidates on Monday, state media reports
data.description:
Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto will submit to parliament the names of two vice presidential candidates later on Monday, state news agency Antara reported, citing an upper house deputy speaker.

The nominations follow the resignation as vice president of Gibran Rakabuming Raka, the son of Prabowo's influential predecessor Joko Widodo, after weeks of political pressure amid legal cases over the validity of Gibran's qualifications in running for the post.

The vice president's position is widely seen as ceremonial in Indonesia and Gibran had little involvement in government decision making.

Analysts say that with Prabowo facing plummeting approval ratings from concerns about the economy and his policies, his choice for vice president could be an important indicator of his political strategy moving ahead.

Deputy house speaker Sohibul Iman confirmed to Antara Prabowo's planned attendance of the house to submit the two names. It was not immediately clear who the candidates are.

Prabowo's office would inform reporters of his attendance at the upper house when confirmed, his spokesperson said.

Gibran's resignation earlier this month is widely seen as a sign of a fraying political partnership between Prabowo and the popular two-term former president Widodo, who is better known as Jokowi, raising the possibility of a significant shift in politics.

The parliament is scheduled on December 11 to select the new vice president through a plenary council after vetting the two candidates.

data.title: Bitcoin Is Correlated With Equities Again — Market Talk
data.description: Bitcoin's relationship with equities has overtaken gold and the dollar as the strongest macro driver in November, Citi's Alex Saunders writes. "Bitcoin's three-month correlation with the S&P 500 has risen above its correlation with gold, which has eased but remains positive, while the relationship with the dollar has become less negative," he says. The issue, Saunders adds, is that the sell-off in crypto has been far larger than the decline in S&P. Higher correlation has not translated into a similar magnitude of price action, he writes. Bitcoin is 1.10% higher at $61,560.15 but down 29.77% year-to-date.(joseph.wilkins@wsj.com)

data.title: Partners Group to Buy New Zealand Transport Firm From Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners
data.description:
By Fabiana Negrin Ochoa

Private-markets firm Partners Group has agreed to acquire a New Zealand transport firm from Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners amid rising client demand for income-oriented infrastructure assets.

Partners Group, which oversees more than $186 billion in assets, said it will invest in StraitNZ from select pools of capital and plans to work with management to further grow the company's recurring revenue base.

No financial terms were disclosed.

StraitNZ is an integrated transport, logistics and ferry company managing freight and passenger services across the Cook Strait. It is one of two ferry operators connecting New Zealand's national highway system from the North Island to the South Island.

Nicholas Kuys, managing director for infrastructure at Partners Group, said the company holds a defensive position on the transport route that's a backbone of the New Zealand economy.

Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners said that since it invested in the company in March 2022, StraitNZ has delivered strong growth in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization.

The deal is in line with Partners Group's expectations that the trend of client demand for strategic brownfield investments will accelerate as more investors recognize the benefits of exposure to such assets.

The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to customary regulatory approvals and other conditions.

Write to Fabiana Negrin Ochoa at fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com

data.title: Australia shares end at six-month low as selloff targets bank stocks
data.description:
Key points:
  • Banks drop 1.2% to lowest level in over 1-month
  • Miners recover; up 1.8% after 13% weekly drop
  • NZ shares skid 2.7%

By Nichiket Sunil

Australian shares fell on Monday, dragged down by major banks as investors weighed a global selloff in AI-linked stocks and domestic economic woes, while New Zealand shares extended losses for a fourth session after hitting a record high last week.

The S&P/ASX 200 closed down 0.3% at 8,570.60 points, its lowest closing level since May 20, after the benchmark plunged more than 5% last week in its worst weekly performance in over four years.

Financial stocks led Monday's losses, falling 1.2% to a more than one-month low after five straight sessions of declines.

The weakness suggested the AI-driven selloff had spread to domestically focused stocks, with concerns that five central bank rate hikes this year could further slow growth.

Unemployment rate hit a five-year high, data showed last week, while consumers faced persistent price pressures and falling household wealth as home prices weakened.

"The shift in selling from miners to banks suggests the market's troubles are spreading beyond the global AI turmoil, with investors increasingly concerned about the strain of elevated interest rates and slowing domestic growth," said Hebe Chen, senior market analyst at Vantage Markets.

Commonwealth Bank of Australia fell 2.2%, ANZ lost 1.7%, while Westpac and National Australia Bank shed 1.9% and 0.6%, respectively.

Miners rebounded 1.8% after plunging nearly 13% last week. BHP rose 2.2% after the world's biggest miner unveiled plans to double copper production in South Australia by 2040 at a cost of up to $17.4 billion.

Rio Tinto gained 1.4%, while gold stocks tracked a recovery in bullion prices.

In New Zealand, the S&P/NZX 50 fell 2.7% to 13,730.25 points, dragged down by a 14% plunge in Gentrack after the technology firm reported sharply lower annual profit.

The index fell for a fourth straight session after hitting a record high of 14,352.72 points last week.

data.title: Oil Inflows to Fujairah Keep Falling as Hormuz Attacks Multiply — Market Talk
data.description: Significantly less oil has made its way out of the Strait of Hormuz in November as U.S.-Iran tensions continue to flare, QuantCube Technology data shows. Inflows to the UAE's Fujairah port--a key proxy to monitor dark Hormuz crossings when ships resurface--are 67% lower than their October peak, says QuantCube economist Alan Lemangnen. Though Fujairah has become a hub for transshipment activities for oil that passes successfully through the vital corridor, longer anchorage times and declining number of ships in the zone provide more evidence of fewer barrels exiting the strait this month, Lemangnen adds.(joseph.wilkins@wsj.com)

data.title: Brookfield to Buy PGP Glass From Blackstone for $1.7 Billion
data.description:
By Fabiana Negrin Ochoa

Brookfield Asset Management has agreed to buy Indian specialty glass packaging maker PGP Glass Blackstone for $1.7 billion, expanding its strategies in Asia.

Brookfield, which manages more than $1 trillion in assets, will buy the Mumbai-based company from funds managed by Blackstone Private Equity.

PGP makes glass packaging for cosmetics, food and beverage, and pharmaceutical companies, and has three manufacturing facilities in India and Sri Lanka. According to its website, customers include Chloe, Bacardi and Nestle.

Cost pressures and capacity rationalization among European and North American manufacturers are creating opportunities for producers such as PGP to expand their market presence, the firms said on Monday.

Brookfield plans to use artificial intelligence to help PGP grow as global demand for high-quality packaging rises, said Aditya Joshi, Brookfield's head of private equity for Asia Pacific and the Middle East.

Brookfield will fund the deal through its flagship Brookfield Capital Partners strategy and affiliate Brookfield Business Corporation. The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027.

Write to Fabiana Negrin Ochoa at fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com

data.title: WULF Stock In Focus As CEO Says He Won't Rush A Muskie Lease Deal In A ‘Terrible Market’
data.description:
Key points:
  • Prager said investor sentiment has been putting pressure on the public markets.
  • He pushed back against pressure to disclose a customer before securing a lease agreement.
  • Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust agreed to purchase a 75% stake in two joint ventures of Amazon Web Services data centers.

TeraWulf (WULF) CEO Paul Prager said on Sunday that the company was not in a hurry to get a tenant for its Muskie data center campus in Kentucky, a deal that would protect shareholders from dilution.

Prager acknowledged the pain of the recent sell-off in U.S. markets, calling it a ‘terrible market’. He wrote on X, “Risk appetite has changed. Public market valuations have changed.” But the demand for compute and the lack of power to support it have not, he added.

No Rush On Muskie

From Prager's perspective, nothing has changed at Muskie. He said the same parties are interested in the gigawatt-scale site. "I don't need to announce a customer just so I can say Muskie is leased," he wrote.

He said the company wants the right customer, credit, economics, and a structure that lets TeraWulf fund its share of the equity. "I hate dilution," Prager wrote.

TeraWulf doubled contracted power at Muskie to 1 GW in October. Now it's about finding the right customer, not just looking at credit, said Prager. Prepayments, customer-funded equipment, and strategic capital would provide the equity needed, he said.

WULF stock was up over 3% in overnight trading, after closing 14% lower on Friday. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around WULF remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, accompanied by ‘normal’ chatter levels over the past day.

The Markets Are Forcing Differentiation

Demand is still strong, said Prager, noting that AMD's (AMD) data center revenue nearly doubled year over year. Some of TeraWulf's customers have discussed accelerating their plans, he added.

On the company's moat, Prager wrote, "Actually, a few customers are talking to us about accelerating. They see the same thing we do: a dysfunctional market can be an opportunity to build a deeper and wider moat."

"The sell-off is making investors separate between real projects and those that have only land and a big megawatt number," he said. Sites with power, permits, and infrastructure already in place are now worth more than they were six months ago, he added.

The Benchmark

Prager called the recent Blackstone-Amazon data center deal "a valuable data point." Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust (BXDC) agreed last week to purchase a 75% stake in two joint ventures of Amazon Web Services data centers for an estimated $5 billion, with a 7% initial cap rate.

He said it was a true example of what long-term investors are willing to pay for consistent data center cash flows backed by strong credit.

WULF has been down 14% so far this year.

data.title: JK Cement agrees solar power offtake from Hero Future Energies
data.description:
November 23 (Renewables Now) - India’s JK Cement Limited (BOM:532644) will buy a 27.03% stake in a company owned by domestic independent power producer (IPP) Hero Future Energies to secure solar power for its Muddapur plant in the state of Karnataka.

The cement maker said on Thursday it will invest INR 51.5 million (USD 555,731/EUR 506,515) to buy 1.1 million shares in Clean Renewable Energy KK 1E, a special purpose vehicle engaged in solar power generation. The stake acquisition is structured as a captive power arrangement that will provide JK Cement with solar electricity for its Muddapur operations.

Clean Renewable Energy KK is promoted by Hero Rooftop Energy, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Hero Future Energies. The entity is involved in the development and operation of a 125.8-MW hybrid project combining 99.4 MW of solar and 26.4 MW of wind power generation.

The captive power purchase will increase the share of renewables in JK Cement’s power mix and support its strategy to strengthen the use of renewable energe usage. Earlier this year, the cement manufacturer secured 70 MWp of solar power supply for its Nimbahera manufacturing facility in Rajasthan through a partnership with Oriana Power.

data.title: Kalyan Jewellers shares jump 5% on news of Rs 2,000-crore fundraising talks with Warburg Pincus, other PE firms
data.description:
Shares of Kalyan Jewellers India surged nearly 5 percent on Monday, November 23, after a Moneycontrol report said the jewellery retailer was in talks with multiple private equity firms, including former investor Warburg Pincus, to raise close to Rs 2,000 crore through minority stake sales in its subsidiaries Candere and Akshaya Thanga Maligai (ATM).

Kalyan Jewellers shares were trading at Rs 668.7 apiece in morning trade, up 4.7 percent, making the stock one of the top midcap gainers. The company's market capitalisation exceeded Rs 69,000 crore. The stock has gained 37.8 percent so far in 2026, significantly outperforming the Nifty 50, which has declined 2.1 percent during the same period.

According to the Moneycontrol report, the proposed fundraising could mark Warburg Pincus's return as an investor in the Kalyan group, more than two years after the global private equity firm completed its exit from the listed jewellery retailer in August 2024.

Warburg Pincus had invested approximately Rs 1,700 crore in Kalyan Jewellers in two rounds between 2014 and 2017, supporting the company's expansion beyond South India into northern and western markets, as well as international markets.

  • Share Markets Live Updates | Sensex, Nifty, GIFT Nifty Today

The latest discussions are aimed at accelerating the expansion of Candere and ATM, two brands catering to different segments of India's jewellery market.

The proposed investment could finance showroom expansion, inventory requirements, product development and brand-building as Kalyan seeks to capitalise on growing demand for lightweight, everyday and fashion-led jewellery while strengthening its traditional regional presence. For Candere, additional capital could accelerate the rollout of physical stores, while ATM could use the funds to expand across Tamil Nadu and potentially other regional markets.

However, the discussions remain preliminary, and the valuations, individual fundraising amounts and stakes proposed to be sold have not been ascertained, the report said.

The fundraising discussions come as Kalyan Jewellers pursues an asset-light expansion strategy through its franchise-owned, company-operated (FOCO) model. Under its FY27 guidance, the company expects its India showroom network to reach 426 outlets, with nearly 306 operating under the FOCO model.

Strong Q2 earnings support investor sentiment

The latest rally follows strong quarterly earnings reported earlier this month, when Kalyan Jewellers posted a 63.6 percent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 427 crore for the September quarter, compared with Rs 260.51 crore a year earlier. The reported profit included an exceptional gain of Rs 73 crore from the sale of a non-core land parcel. Excluding this gain, net profit stood at approximately Rs 354 crore, representing growth of nearly 36 percent.

Consolidated revenue rose 31.4 percent to Rs 10,323 crore from Rs 7,856 crore in the year-ago quarter, crossing the Rs 10,000-crore mark. Following the results, brokerage firm UBS maintained its Buy rating on Kalyan Jewellers, with a target price of Rs 900 per share.

data.title: ALS Ltd. H1 Profit Surges, Lifts FY27 Organic Revenue Growth View; But Stock Drops
data.description:
CANBERA (dpa-AFX) - ALS Limited (CPBLF, ALQ.AX), an Australian testing, inspection, and certification company, reported Monday significantly higher profit for its first half of fiscal 2027, with increased revenues. Further, the company raised fiscal 2027 organic growth view for Group and Minerals, but trimmed growth outlook for Life Sciences.

In Australia, the shares were losing around 13.41%, trading at $16.71.

In the first half, net profit after tax was $297.5 million, up 110% from last year's $141.7 million. The latest result included a $97.2 million non-cash fair value gain on the existing investment in Saudi Arabia.

Underlying net profit was $214.6 million, compared to $173.6 million a year ago. Underlying basic earnings per share increased 21.6% to 42.3 cents from prior year's 34.8 cents.

Underlying EBIT of $332.7 million climbed 18.6% from $280.5 million, and underlying EBIT margin expanded by 250 basis points to 19.4%. Margin expansion was driven by strong Commodities volume growth, pricing discipline, and continued cost control across both divisions, the company said.

Revenue of $1.72 billion grew 3.4% from last year's $1.66 billion. The growth was 9.6% on constant currency basis, with strong organic revenue growth in Commodities contrasting softer growth in Life Sciences.

Organic growth was 10.2% on a constant currency basis.

Further, the firm announced interim dividend of 23.3 cents per share, to be payable on December 21, to shareholders of record on December 1.

Looking ahead for fiscal 2027, the Group now targets high-single digit organic revenue growth and margin expansion.

The company previously expected mid to high single-digit organic revenue growth across the Group and margin expansion similar to prior year's improvement rate.

Minerals organic revenue growth would now be around 20%, compared to previous view of 13% to 15% increase. Life Sciences organic revenue growth is now expected at around 3%, with a return to mid-single digit growth in the second half. The previous view was improved mid-single digit organic revenue growth.

data.title: AI, caramba!
data.description:
A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Rae Wee

It's been a bruising November for the AI faithful, with markets from Taiwan and South Korea to the US staring at steep monthly losses as the selloff in tech and chip stocks at the heart of the AI boom shows little sign of letting up.

Investors are questioning whether vast sums of mostly borrowed money spent building data centres to power AI tools will generate returns fast enough to repay lenders or big enough to justify some of the high stock prices.

Add to that the departure of Nvidia's influential figurehead Jensen Huang, an intensifying US-China tech war and the prospect of greater scrutiny over the data centre buildout following the Democrats' sweeping midterm victory, and the AI trade is looking increasingly shaky.

US futures bounced on Monday following last week's wipeout but selling pressure remained in Asia, with trading thinned by a holiday in Japan.

The scale of the selloff has once again caught the attention of policymakers in South Korea and Taiwan — the region's AI bellwethers.

South Korea's finance minister on Monday reiterated plans to stabilise the market, if necessary. Taiwan's financial regulator has ordered a tightening of short-selling rules for stocks, while in China, stock exchanges announced a batch of support measures such as easing requirements for margin financing.

As Goldman Sachs' Tony Pasquariello puts it: "The market has shown its hand regarding its dependency on the AI story.

"After nearly four years of uninterrupted advancement — during which time the AI theme was rocket fuel for the market and, thus, the wealth effect — we've entered a far more complicated period."

The next key catalyst that could determine whether the selloff snowballs further will be Wednesday's release of the US personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, a key inflation gauge that could offer clues on how much further the Federal Reserve may need to raise rates.

Expectations of a 25-basis-point Fed hike next month have kept the dollar perched near a 19-month high, with the global stocks rout lending the greenback an additional safe-haven bid.

Separately, MSCI CEO Henry Fernandez conveyed a willingness to consider alternatives to a two-step downgrade of Indonesia's stock-market status in recent talks with President Prabowo Subianto, Bloomberg News reported, citing people with knowledge of the discussion.

Key developments that could influence markets on Monday:

- France, Germany, euro zone S&P flash manufacturing, services PMI (November)

- UK flash manufacturing, services PMI (November)

- New York Fed President John Williams speaks
